notes: Light labial stop. Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

Heavy labial stop. Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Voicing is not distinctive; the stops have 'prompt onset of voicing for the following vowel and no aspiration' (pp. 35-36). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light labial nasal. Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Heavy labial nasal. Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light dental stop. Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). With 'a bit of frication in its release' (p. 37). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Heavy dental stop. Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light dental nasal. Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Heavy dental nasal. Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded dental nasal, 'a rare sound in Marshallese' (p. 28). Rounded (velarized and labialized): heavy, with the lips protruded and pursed (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
(Heavy) velar stop; there are no light velars (p. 25). It closes 'against the same part of the velum whether vowels are front or back' (p. 37). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded velar stop. Rounded (velarized and labialized): heavy, with the lips protruded and pursed (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
(Heavy) velar nasal, transcribed {g}. Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded velar nasal. Rounded (velarized and labialized): heavy, with the lips protruded and pursed (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light lateral. Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

Heavy lateral: the tongue tip against the back of the upper teeth or the gum ridge, open at the sides (p. 24). Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded lateral. Rounded (velarized and labialized): heavy, with the lips protruded and pursed (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light retroflex, spelled d (p. 21). Light (palatalized): the oral tube kept as short as possible (pp. 20-21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

Heavy retroflex: the tongue curled back and trilled 'against the gum ridge behind the upper teeth' (p. 24). Heavy (velarized): 'the back of the tongue is raised' toward the velum (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded retroflex. Rounded (velarized and labialized): heavy, with the lips protruded and pursed (p. 21). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Light semiconsonant {y}, not written in the spelling (pp. 34-35). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

Heavy semiconsonant {h}: the tongue root drawn back and the back of the tongue raised toward the velum, 'not as breathy as the English h' (pp. 34-35). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
Rounded semiconsonant: {h} with lip rounding added (pp. 34-35). Table 2-1 (p. 25); IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

The high vowel phoneme {i} (§2.3.1, pp. 39-42). Height is the only distinctive dimension of the vowels: 'whether a vowel has a front or back sound ... and whether a back vowel is rounded or not ... are determined by the consonants on either side' (p. 39). IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

The high-mid 'derived' vowel {ẹ}, from a combination of {i} and {e} (§2.5.3); it contrasts with both (ki {kiy} 'key' : ke {kẹy} 'porpoise' : ke {key} 'when') but is spelled like {e} and is 'unstable', interchanging with {e} between dialects and speakers (Rālik {ṃẹk} : Ratak {ṃek} 'tired') (§2.3.4, pp. 48-49). Height is the only distinctive dimension of the vowels: 'whether a vowel has a front or back sound ... and whether a back vowel is rounded or not ... are determined by the consonants on either side' (p. 39). IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

The mid vowel phoneme {e} (§2.3.2, pp. 43-44). Height is the only distinctive dimension of the vowels: 'whether a vowel has a front or back sound ... and whether a back vowel is rounded or not ... are determined by the consonants on either side' (p. 39). IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.

The low vowel phoneme {a} (§2.3.3, pp. 45-46). Height is the only distinctive dimension of the vowels: 'whether a vowel has a front or back sound ... and whether a back vowel is rounded or not ... are determined by the consonants on either side' (p. 39). IPA per decision bender2016-ipa.
